summary: A crow's-nest lookout on Pat Knoll in the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest, known from a 1917 fire report; the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as gone.

facts.design: crow's nest, per the Forest Fire Lookout Association list
facts.status_note: Listed as a crow's nest that is now gone. No source we read gives a removal date or describes what remains at the site.

access.note: Forest Road 90 leads to the summit and is unpaved. A road guide says heavy snow makes it impassable, so it is seasonally closed in winter, and advises checking for gate closures. No source describes the summit site itself.

events.note: Ellis Wiltbank named as the Pat Knoll lookout in May 1917
Fire spotted from the supervisor's office in Springerville; the Pat Knoll station phoned it in with two other lookouts; about 100 acres burned before control

resolved_conflicts.explanation: TopoQuest gives the summit at 9,484 ft and Dangerous Roads gives 9,379 ft. The story reports both and does not pick one.

sources.title: Pat Knoll: Driving Forest Road 90 in the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The only history found is one 1917 newspaper account, quoted second-hand by Forest Lookouts. No build year, no removal date and no photo. Do not confuse with PS Knoll (us-az-ps-knoll), a different site with different coordinates. The brief's coordinates sit about 1.4 km from the TopoQuest summit point; left unchanged. Worth trying: Springerville and Morenci newspaper archives for 1917 and later years, and Apache-Sitgreaves forest history files.
